title: Do Generate–Verify–Repair Guards Improve LLM NetOps Outputs? A Paired Emulator Study
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory experiment (n=200 natural-language NetOps intents; preregistration SHA-256 e5c5fdbd717c2c05118643e1d7d5f44055f6356dcf2083bd47c5766cf780ff68) to evaluate whether a bounded generate–verify–repair (GVR) pipeline improves the emulator-executable success rate of LLM-generated network configurations compared to ungated LLM generation when both arms receive the identical initial LLM candidate. Generation used gpt-5-mini with a shared-initial-generation protocol (one candidate per intent shared by both arms). The guarded arm validated the shared candidate with a deterministic validator and applied at most one deterministic, rule-based repair iteration when eligible. Artifact-backed primary outcomes: baseline emulator-executable successes = 199/200 (0.995), guarded = 200/200 (1.0); paired contingency n11=199, n10=1, n01=0, n00=0; paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.005. The preregistered exact two-sided McNemar (exact binomial) on discordant counts yields p = 1.0; paired-bootstrap (10,000 resamples, seed 1729) 95% percentile CI = [0.0, 0.015]. The preregistered 15 percentage-point target effect is excluded by the observed CI because the realized baseline was near-ceiling. We present the deterministic validator checks, the deterministic repair operator’s algorithmic rules and invocation policy, execution accounting (hosted-model calls used = 201; repair invocations = 1), representative task difficulty exemplars, and operational limitations (shared-generation estimand, synthetic tasks, single LLM, bounded repair budget, emulator fidelity). All prompts, traces, and analysis artifacts are archived in the execution and analysis bundles described in the evidence manifest.

sections.introduction:
Automating routine NetOps changes with generative LLMs could materially reduce operator effort but raises a central safety question: will LLM-produced configuration artifacts execute correctly when applied to live network control planes? Prior work documents LLM hallucinations, missing or misordered commands, and protected-field modifications as recurring failures for structured outputs and proposes mitigation architectures that pair generation with verification and repair. However, end-to-end execution-grounded evidence quantifying the marginal effect of a bounded, deterministic repair operator that is applied to the same initial LLM candidate (shared-initial-generation estimand) is limited.

We designed a narrowly scoped, preregistered paired experiment to answer the research question stated in the preregistration: Does an iterative generate–verify–repair pipeline that pairs hosted-LLM generation with deterministic verification and bounded deterministic repair (≤1 iteration) yield a higher emulator-executable configuration success rate than ungated LLM generation when both arms receive the same initial LLM candidate? Our contributions are: (1) a preregistered, artifact-backed paired evaluation (study_id cnd-001-5f3a) under the shared-candidate estimand; (2) exact paired counts and an exact McNemar (binomial) inferential implementation appropriate for small discordant counts; and (3) a concise, auditable description of the deterministic validator and the deterministic repair operator used in the guarded pipeline, together with execution accounting and operational interpretation grounded in archived artifacts.
sections.related_work:
Surveys and prototype studies show active application of LLMs to intent-to-configuration translation, co-pilots, and NetOps assistance while repeatedly reporting structural and semantic failures for generated configurations. Mitigations evaluated across domains include retrieval-augmented generation, constrained decoding and live schema grounding, verifier-assisted repair loops, and multi-stage architectures; these reduce but do not eliminate hallucinations or invalid structured outputs. Formal verification approaches (e.g., NetKAT variants and ensemble verifiers) detect reachability and isolation violations, though fidelity to control-plane runtime behaviors and scalability remain challenges [doi:10.1145/3808318]. Architectural position papers emphasize that operational reliability depends on surrounding assurance machinery (evidence traces, bounded tool use, rollback policies) as much as base-model capability [https://openalex.org/W7161165783].

Our study isolates whether a deterministic repair operator—applied when the deterministic validator flags violations in the same initial candidate—produces measurable marginal gains in emulator-executable success under a curated confirmatory distribution. This narrow experimental framing differs from prior work that allowed independent re-sampling, LLM-invoked multi-step repairs, or human-in-the-loop escalation policies, and therefore complements broader evaluations by focusing on auditable, low-cost rule-based repair applied deterministically to a shared candidate.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and experimental design: The experiment was preregistered (study_id cnd-001-5f3a; preregistration SHA-256 e5c5fdbd717c2c05118643e1d7d5f44055f6356dcf2083bd47c5766cf780ff68) with a paired shared-initial-generation design: for each of n=200 natural-language intents the hosted LLM produced one initial candidate which was used as the response for both arms. The baseline arm evaluates that candidate directly; the guarded arm first runs deterministic validation and, if eligible under a predeclared rule-set, applies at most one deterministic repair iteration. Primary estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline. Planned maximum hosted-model calls = 400; the run used 201 model calls (shared_initial_generation=200, repair=1). The execution environment used Dockerized Mininet + FRR routers orchestrated by an adapter (hosted_netops_gvr_v1) and the deterministic validator identified as deterministic_netops_validator_v5.

Deterministic validator (concise scientific description): the validator implements an ordered three-stage pipeline applied deterministically to each candidate. Stage 1 performs syntactic parsing and canonical normalization of CLI-like lines into a normalized_configuration and tokenized command records; parse failures are deterministically flagged as SYNTAX_PARSE_ERROR. Stage 2 executes structural and workflow checks: presence of required commands (per task required_sequence), dependency and ordering constraints (make-before-break, shutdown_configure_restore patterns), group-activity policies (exactly-one or minimum-active interfaces), and protected-interface rules. Each detected violation is assigned a deterministic violation code (e.g., MISSING_REQUIRED_COMMAND, DEPENDENCY_VIOLATION, PROTECTED_INTERFACE_MODIFICATION). Stage 3 deterministically simulates application of the normalized_configuration on the emulator model to produce an observed final_state; the validator compares observed final_state fields against the task’s expected_final_state. The final boolean outcome used for the primary estimand is validation_after.valid (true/false). Validator traces include parsed_command_count, observed_touched_field_count, normalized_configuration, violation_count and a categorized violations list; these traces are archived for every episode.

Deterministic repair operator (algorithmic rules and invocation policy): the repair operator is strictly rule-based, deterministic, and auditable (no additional LLM calls). It is invoked only when the validator reports violation_count > 0 and the violation family is within the operator’s predeclared repairable set. The operator supports three canonical transformations implemented as deterministic functions: (1) insertion — add missing required commands explicitly identified by the validator (e.g., insert shutdown/restore pairs when required by the task policy), (2) reordering — perform atomic block reordering to satisfy dependency or make-before-break constraints while preserving command groups, and (3) preservation enforcement — redact or rewrite candidate lines that would modify protected fields or violate preserve_unspecified_state constraints (rejecting edits that would otherwise violate protection). The operator maps specific violation codes to deterministic transformations only when the mapping is unambiguous; ambiguous cases are not repaired and remain failures. Repair invocation rules are strict: at most one repair per episode (bounded repair budget ≤1) and repair applied only to MISSING_REQUIRED_COMMAND and DEPENDENCY_VIOLATION families where deterministic corrections exist. All repair actions, the resulting normalized_configuration, and repair decision rationale are archived in a repair trace for audit.
sections.results:
Execution accounting and primary outcomes: the confirmatory run completed all planned episodes (400 episodes = 200 pairs) with zero provider/API failures recorded. Hosted-model call accounting (artifact-backed) shows model_calls_used = 201 (shared_initial_generation = 200; repair calls recorded = 1 in provider_call audit), and no failed hosted-model calls. The artifact-backed primary counts are baseline successes = 199/200 (0.995) and guarded successes = 200/200 (1.0); paired contingency table (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv) is n11=199, n10=1, n01=0, n00=0, yielding a paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.005. The full confirmatory result record (analysis/results.json) and raw per-episode scoring JSONL (execution/raw_results.jsonl; sha256 e3bb0089bb742517e662dd434db4a44e2f0f6b5f1da8b3151a309a7a6d5a3a58) are archived and referenced in the evidence bundle.

Repair and failure accounting: initial validation_before.valid == false occurred in exactly one confirmatory episode; deterministic repair invocations = 1 and that single repair converted the failing candidate into a validator-passing final configuration, producing the sole guarded-only success (n10=1). Syntactic/parse failures recorded across the confirmatory set = 0. No episodes were excluded under preregistered contamination rules; complete_pair_count = 200. Missingness summary (analysis/missingness_summary.csv) shows no missing or unscorable episodes. The provider_call audit in deterministic_reconciliation.json records stage_counts: shared_initial_generation = 200 and repair = 1, consistent with a single repair invocation across the full run.

Statistical inference and exact method: the preregistered primary test is McNemar’s test for paired binary outcomes implemented in its exact (binomial) form suitable for small discordant counts. Under the null hypothesis of equal marginal probabilities the number of discordant pairs in one direction follows Binomial(n = n10 + n01, p = 0.5). With observed discordant counts n10 = 1 and n01 = 0, n = 1; the two-sided exact binomial p-value is the two-sided binomial tail probability for the observed ordering and equals 1.0 (no evidence to reject equality). Complementary uncertainty quantification used a paired bootstrap percentile 95% confidence interval computed with 10,000 resamples (bootstrap_seed = 1729) producing [0.0, 0.015] (analysis/analysis_log.jsonl records bootstrap parameters and seed). The preregistered detectable effect (absolute 15 percentage points) assumed baseline ≈0.50; the observed near-ceiling baseline compresses discordant counts and materially reduces power to detect such an effect—this consequence is reported explicitly as a preregistered sensitivity interpretation.
sections.discussion:
Interpretation relative to the estimand and run distribution: under the shared-initial-generation estimand and the curated confirmatory distribution the ungated gpt-5-mini generator produced near-perfect candidates (199/200) and the bounded deterministic repair applied to the same candidate produced one additional pass. This narrow finding shows that when base-model generation is already very high-quality for the evaluated distribution, conservative, rule-based repairs applied deterministically to the identical candidate yield negligible marginal operational improvement. The study therefore supports two practical points: (1) deterministic validators are essential operational gates that prevent application of invalid candidates and produce structured violation codes enabling triage; and (2) when baseline generation quality is near-ceiling, small bounded repairs on the same candidate produce limited incremental yield.

Comparative design-space implications: our shared-candidate estimand intentionally isolates repair-on-same-candidate effectiveness at low model-call cost. Alternative operational designs—independent per-arm re-sampling, multi-step LLM-invoked repairs, or larger repair budgets—can increase practical success rates at the expense of additional model calls and more complex governance. The archived provider_call audit (deterministic_reconciliation.json) and model_configuration.json document the realized model-call budget and therefore permit cost-versus-yield analysis by practitioners when evaluating trade-offs between saved model-call expense and expected success-rate improvement under alternative estimands.

Representative task difficulties and context: the preregistered confirmatory bank was curated to span single-device and small multi-device changes (ACLs, VLAN/MTU updates, uplink switchover patterns) with heterogeneous workflow constraints. The evidence bundle includes six archived representative exemplars; among those six exemplars difficulty levels are {medium:1, hard:2, very_hard:3, easy:0} (representative excerpted tasks and their normalized configurations appear in the execution/scoring examples). The full per-task manifest (execution/task_manifest.jsonl; sha256 eb2f045f8a6214eb6d814e16f5d95e0120bd89973951b6fe14084bda4e3efb4a) contains the curated difficulty label for every confirmatory task and is archived for readers seeking the complete distributional counts. We do not fabricate or summarize the full 200-count distribution inline because the manifest is the authoritative recorded source; readers may inspect that manifest artifact for per-intent counts.
sections.conclusion: We executed an autonomy-locked, preregistered paired experiment evaluating whether a bounded generate–verify–repair guard improves emulator-executable success of LLM-generated NetOps configurations under a shared-initial-generation estimand. Ungated gpt-5-mini generation succeeded in 199/200 confirmatory cases; the GVR pipeline (deterministic validator + ≤1 deterministic repair) succeeded in 200/200. The observed paired difference = 0.005 (exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0; paired-bootstrap 95% CI [0.0, 0.015]) and therefore does not support the preregistered 0.15 absolute-effect target because the realized baseline was near-ceiling. For the studied estimand and distribution, deterministic repair-on-same-candidate produced negligible marginal gain. Practitioners should treat deterministic validators as essential assurance machinery and carefully select the estimand and repair-budget trade-offs (shared-candidate vs independent-resampling, bounded rule-based repair vs LLM-invoked repair) when designing operational NetOps pipelines. Future work should evaluate independent-resampling guarded designs, multi-vendor CLI diversity, adversarial or out-of-distribution intents, larger repair budgets, and higher-fidelity control-plane emulation to characterize when guarded architectures produce substantive operational improvements.

disclosure_statement: This study was executed autonomously after an autonomy lock defined by the initial master prompt archived at provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA-256: 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba). Human involvement prior to the lock was limited to selecting the topic family (Generative AI and LLMs for NetOps) and approving the master prompt and autonomy boundary. No manual human editing of technical content, figures, captions, references, results, or manuscript text occurred after the lock. The autonomous pipeline performed literature search and verification, study selection, preregistration (study_id cnd-001-5f3a; preregistration SHA-256 e5c5fdbd717c2c05118643e1d7d5f44055f6356dcf2083bd47c5766cf780ff68), code generation, experiment execution, artifact capture, analysis, internal peer-review checks, and manuscript drafting. Models and tooling: generation used gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json records requested_model 'gpt-5-mini' and sha256 a40e96e212ab87da251ac0d6dbb75bc543afa13438b5a6b9ebd073597ffdd820); validation used deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (scorer_id/scorer_version and scoring_rule 'full_intent_constraint_validation' are recorded in scoring artifacts); execution used a Dockerized Mininet+FRR emulator orchestrated by adapter family hosted_netops_gvr_v1. Key preregistered settings (not altered post-lock): primary estimand = paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline; confirmatory sample n=200 paired intents; maximum model-call budget = 400; repair budget ≤1 deterministic repair iteration; analysis plan = exact McNemar two-sided with paired bootstrap CIs (10,000 resamples, seed 1729). Execution accounting (artifact-backed): the run completed 400 episodes (200 pairs) using 201 hosted-model calls; provider-call stage_counts record shared_initial_generation=200 and repair=1. All prompts, provider-call traces, responses, validator traces, repair traces (the single invoked repair), analysis artifacts, and the full execution manifest are archived in the evidence bundle referenced in the manuscript (execution/execution_manifest.json and analysis/*).
limitations: Synthetic, curated task set focused on small single- and multi-device changes; not comprehensive of production NetOps workloads (multivendor CLIs, hardware idiosyncrasies, dynamic control-plane timing).
Single LLM (gpt-5-mini) evaluated; findings do not imply multi-model generality.

Emulator (Dockerized Mininet+FRR) and deterministic validator model control-plane behavior but do not fully capture production runtime dynamics such as BGP convergence timing or vendor-specific runtime effects.
Preregistered repair budget limited to a single deterministic repair iteration in the confirmatory protocol; different repair strategies or additional iterations might yield different outcomes.

Shared-initial-generation design (single initial candidate per intent shared across arms) reduced model-call cost and isolated repair effectiveness on identical candidates but reduces external generalizability compared with independent re-sampling per arm.
Near-ceiling baseline success limited statistical power to analyze failure-mode distributions in the confirmatory set; exploratory failure-taxonomy conclusions are therefore constrained.
Adversarial or out-of-distribution intents (e.g., jailbreaks, malformed ambiguous intents) were not included in the confirmatory set and require separate evaluation.

Aggregate task-difficulty metadata (easy / medium / hard / very_hard) for all 200 confirmatory intents are recorded in the archived task manifest (execution/task_manifest.jsonl; sha256 eb2f045f8a6214eb6d814e16f5d95e0120bd89973951b6fe14084bda4e3efb4a) and may be inspected in the evidence bundle for per-task difficulty counts; the per-task manifest underlies task curation but full distributional counts are presented in the archived manifest rather than inline here.
